headline: Google and the FBI dismantled NetNut, a residential proxy network built from two million hijacked home devices, as commercial Pegasus spyware surfaced on the phone of the very European lawmaker who once investigated it.

emerging_trends.text: A joint Google and FBI operation degraded the NetNut residential proxy network, part of a widening law-enforcement push to strip criminals and nation-state actors of the anonymizing infrastructure they rent.
Mac users drew fresh fire as PamStealer disguised itself as the Maccy clipboard tool, extending a surge of infostealers built to crack macOS login passwords.
Commercial spyware keeps striking the people meant to police it, with Pegasus turning up on the phone of a European Parliament member who had spent his term investigating its abuse.

topics.title: NetNut Residential Proxy Network Seized
topics.latest_developments: Google's Threat Intelligence Group and the FBI, working with Lumen, seized hundreds of NetNut domains on July 2 and cut millions of devices from the network, roughly two weeks after KrebsOnSecurity tied NetNut to the Popa botnet.
topics.summary: NetNut, also tracked as Popa and run by the publicly traded Israeli firm Alarum Technologies (NASDAQ: ALAR), rented access to at least two million compromised home devices so cybercriminals and nation-state actors could mask their traffic. The takedown degraded the pool of usable relays worldwide.

sources.title: FBI Seizes NetNut Proxy Platform, Popa Botnet
Google, FBI Disrupt NetNut Residential Proxy Network Powered by Millions of Devices
Google Disrupts NetNut Residential Proxy Network Spanning 2 Million Home Devices

topics.title: Pegasus Infects Spyware Investigator's Phone
topics.latest_developments: Citizen Lab reported July 3 that forensic analysis found NSO Group's Pegasus spyware on the phone of Stelios Kouloglou twice while he served on the European Parliament committee investigating commercial spyware abuse.
topics.summary: Kouloglou, a former Greek member of the European Parliament's PEGA committee, sat on the very body tasked with probing surveillance-tool abuse across the bloc when attackers compromised his device. Fellow lawmakers called the infection a direct attack on the rule of law.

sources.title: European Parliament Member Investigating Spyware Was Hacked With Pegasus
EU Politicians Investigated Pegasus Spyware. Then It Ended Up on One of Their Phones
Spyware found on phone of European Parliament member probing it

topics.title: PamStealer Targets macOS Login Passwords
topics.latest_developments: Jamf Threat Labs disclosed PamStealer, a macOS infostealer shipped as a compiled AppleScript file that impersonates the open-source clipboard manager Maccy and abuses pluggable authentication module checks to capture Mac login passwords.
topics.summary: PamStealer spreads through fake Maccy download sites, then siphons credentials and sensitive data while evading scrutiny. The find underscores mounting investment in Mac-focused infostealers.

sources.title: PamStealer Uses Fake Maccy Sites and PAM Checks to Steal Mac Login Passwords
Newly discovered PamStealer isn't your typical macOS malware

topics.title: ARToken Phishing Kit Hits Microsoft 365
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer detailed ARToken on July 3, a phishing-as-a-service platform operating as an affiliate of the EvilTokens service, exposing an extensive toolkit built to compromise Microsoft 365 accounts.
topics.summary: ARToken lowers the bar for stealing Microsoft 365 credentials and session tokens through ready-made phishing infrastructure. Organizations should enforce phishing-resistant multifactor authentication and monitor for anomalous token use.

sources.title: ARToken PhaaS exposes EvilTokens' Microsoft 365 phishing toolkit

topics.title: Medtronic Breach Exposes 3.8 Million
topics.latest_developments: Medtronic disclosed July 3 that ShinyHunters breached its corporate IT systems in April and stole the personal and medical information of 3.8 million patients.
topics.summary: The medical-device maker Medtronic joins a growing roster of ShinyHunters victims. Affected patients face exposure of health records; the company is notifying those involved.

sources.title: Medtronic Data Breach Impacts 3.8 Million People

topics.title: Anubis Ransomware Exploits Citrix Bleed 2
topics.latest_developments: The Hacker News reported July 2 that Anubis ransomware affiliates now exploit Citrix Bleed 2 (CVE-2025-5777) for initial access, then pair legitimate remote-monitoring tools, bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver techniques, and stolen supply-chain credentials for hands-on-keyboard intrusions.
topics.summary: Anubis operators bypass NetScaler defenses through the Citrix Bleed 2 information-disclosure flaw and lean on trusted RMM software to move quietly. Administrators running Citrix NetScaler should confirm the CVE-2025-5777 patch and hunt for rogue RMM activity.

sources.title: Ransomware Groups Turn to Citrix Bleed 2, BYOVD, and Supply Chain Credentials

business_politics.title: Weak U.S. Jobs Data Sink the Dollar
business_politics.latest_developments: Thursday's worse-than-expected June nonfarm payrolls pushed the dollar to a weekly low on July 3, lifted gold, and drove a risk-on rally through global stocks as traders unwound rate-hike bets.
business_politics.summary: The U.S. June employment report undershot forecasts, weakening the dollar against major currencies, sending gold higher, and cooling expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise rates; with U.S. markets closed for Independence Day, the moves rippled through European and Asian trading.

business.summary: Premium gasoline has widened its price gap over regular as more U.S. drivers, many in newer vehicles that require higher octane, choose it at the pump, pushing premium costs up.

around_town.summary: The West End Circle, the heavily traveled interchange tying the West End Bridge to Route 51 and the neighborhoods below, will close overnight next week while crews complete utility work.

around_town.latest_developments: WTAE reported July 3 that, ahead of the Parkway East closure, PennDOT is urging drivers to use its 511PA website and app for real-time detour planning.
around_town.summary: PennDOT is directing motorists to 511PA, its free real-time traffic website and app, to navigate detours during the coming closure of the Parkway East, Interstate 376, in Pittsburgh's East End.

around_town.title: Heat Wave Adds Storms Through the Holiday Weekend
around_town.latest_developments: KDKA reported July 3 that a fourth straight day of 90-degree heat now carries thunderstorm chances, with well-timed storms possibly derailing Saturday's highs.
around_town.summary: Western Pennsylvania's extreme-heat warning held for a fourth straight day July 3 with feels-like temperatures above 100 degrees, and forecasters added severe-storm chances Friday through Sunday across the Fourth of July weekend.

events.title: Pittsburgh Symphony Budget Jumps to $42 Million
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported July 1 that the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra's annual budget leapt by $7 million to $42 million, driven largely by its film-music work.
events.summary: The Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra's budget has grown by $7 million to $42 million, an increase the Post-Gazette attributes largely to the orchestra's expanding business recording and performing film scores.

sources.title: Analysis: Here's why the Pittsburgh Symphony's budget just jumped by $7 million to $42 million

events.title: Pittsburgh's Record July 4 Fireworks
events.latest_developments: WTAE reported July 3 that Pittsburgh has added drone surveillance, increased security, and parental advisories for Saturday's America 250 Fourth of July celebration.
events.summary: Pittsburgh's Fourth of July celebration Saturday, July 4, billed as the largest fireworks show in city history for the nation's 250th birthday, will carry heightened downtown security, drone surveillance, and parental advisories for an expected record crowd.

sources.title: Pittsburgh enhances safety measures for July 4 celebrations

around_teams.summary: Post-Gazette columnist Noah Hiles examined the causes of Pirates ace Paul Skenes' recent struggles, weighing blame among Skenes himself, his catchers, and pitching coaches after a run of bumpy starts capped by a career-high eight runs against the Phillies.

around_teams.summary: The Pirates will send two of their top prospects, pitcher Seth Hernandez and Edward Florentino, to the All-Star Futures Game, an exhibition of the sport's rising minor leaguers held during All-Star week.

team_usa.title: U.S. Olympian Indicted in Reflecting Pool Case
team_usa.latest_developments: A grand jury in Washington indicted three-time U.S. Olympic canoeist David Hearn on July 2 on a felony charge tied to damage at the Reflecting Pool.
team_usa.summary: David Hearn, a 67-year-old three-time U.S. Olympic canoeist, was indicted on a felony charge accusing him of maliciously breaking lining material at Washington's Reflecting Pool, which President Trump had blamed on vandals after a $14.7 million renovation.
